name: foundry-lan-control-plane-v2
mission: Make the current single-daemon architecture practical as a trusted-LAN control plane. Registry and campaign state are already daemon-authoritative; the CLI currently has an explicit --addr flag with a fixed loopback default, and foundryd still binds unconditionally to 127.0.0.1:50051. Add a configurable daemon listen address, a persistent client daemon-address default with explicit --addr precedence, plaintext remote operation, and an exact no-split-brain migration runbook for moving authority from the Mac to mojility-ops-01 after all remaining state-domain campaigns close. Preserve loopback defaults. Authentication, TLS, clustering, and the live migration itself remain out of scope.

done_evidence.command: cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace

done_evidence.statement: foundryd supports a startup-configured listen address while preserving the 127.0.0.1:50051 default, and integration tests prove binding a non-default address and serving a remote-style plaintext gRPC client.

The CLI supports a persistent environment or configuration daemon-address default, an explicit --addr override takes precedence, and the loopback default remains unchanged when neither is set. Tests pin the full precedence order.
Documentation identifies plaintext trusted-LAN operation as an explicit deployment choice and does not imply authentication, TLS, clustering, or multiple writable authorities.

A migration runbook inventories every authoritative Foundry state path, requires registry, campaign, sentinel, and observability authority campaigns to be complete before cutover, performs a one-time copy to mojility-ops-01, validates remote command parity, prevents both daemons from being writable simultaneously, and defines rollback before retiring the Mac daemon.

escalation: The endpoint design requires choosing authentication, TLS, or clustering policy.
The Mac and mojility-ops-01 contain divergent authoritative state requiring a merge decision.
A migration step would make both daemons writable at the same time.
The same objective fails required validation twice.
The agent provider is unavailable because of authentication, rate, or spend capacity.
